delta: # Story 33 — Web language switch flips the inter

face without a reload (Story: CRM-37)

## Prerequisites

- **LANGUAGES-1-WEB (CRM-35)** completed: the two dictionaries in `web/src/shared
/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` and `I18nProvider` in `web/src/shared/i18n/index.tsx` are already in place, and `<html dir>`

/ `<html lang>` are already driven from a single effect there.
- **PLATFORM theming story (CRM-27)** completed: `web/src/app/theme-context.ts

x` and its test are the shape this story copies. Do **not** invent a second pattern.
- Co
ordinate naming only (no code change) with **LANGUAGES-2-MOB (CRM-38)** and **LANGUAGES-3-WEB (CRM-39)** — they are

out of scope here.

---

## Story Goal

The signed-in agent can switch the interface from English to Arabic (and back) from a control in the desk shell header. The swit
ch changes text, writing direction and alignment **in the same render**, without a route change or page
reload. The chosen language is remembered across reloads. Direction still comes from `<html dir>` and CSS logical properties — no second st

ylesheet mirrors the layout by hand.

**In scope:** stateful `I18nProvider`, persistence in `localStorage`, a header button in `DeskShell

`, two new dictionary keys, a lint-style guard test that forbids `[dir=` selectors and physical direction properties in `web/src` CSS.

**Not
in scope:** Android (CRM-38), locale-formatted dates/numbers (CRM-39), missing-key checker (CRM-40), any third language, run-time locale loading, chang

ing the theme provider, altering shell layout, or translating any new copy beyond the switcher's two labels.

---

## Context — Read These Files First

1
. `web/src/app/theme-context.tsx` — the whole file (71 lines). This is the precedent. Note `THEME_KEY` (line 5), `THEMES` +
`isTheme` guard (lines 7–9), `readStoredTheme` with `try/catch` around `globalThis.localStorage?.getItem` (lines 15–29), the **synchronous** `useState
<Theme>(readStoredTheme)` initialiser (line 35), `setTheme` that writes storage first then state (lines 37–44), and the `useEffect` that applies the value to

`document.documentElement` (lines 46–51). The new language provider mirrors every one of these decisions.
2. `web/src/app/theme-context.test.tsx` — read end
-to-end for the test pattern (private-window `localStorage` stub that throws, unrecognised stored value falls back, toggle after

two quick clicks, `<html>` attribute assertion). The language test mirrors it.
3. `web/src/shared/i18n/index.tsx` — the whole file (46 lines). `Language`
, `Direction`, `dictionaries`, `directions`, `I18nProvider({ language = 'en', children })` (lines 18–24), `useMemo`
of `{ language, t, dir }` (lines 25–28), the `useEffect` at lines 30–37 that sets `<html dir>` **and** `<html lang>`,

and `useTranslation` (lines 42–46). Keep the `language` prop as an **initial-value override** — do not remove it.
4. `web/src/app/desk-
shell/DeskShell.tsx` — lines 1–53. See how the theme control is rendered (lines 21–31): `useTheme()
` returns `theme` + `toggleTheme`, a label is chosen from `t.shell.switchToLight | switchToDark`, and a `

<Button variant="secondary">` is placed inside the header `Stack`. The language switcher slots into the same `Stack`, immediately before the theme button.
5. `web/src/testing/
render.tsx` — lines 1–55. Note the comment at lines 11–19 ("mirrors app/App.tsx exactly is
load-bearing") and the `language` option threaded into `<I18nProvider language={language}>` at line 42. The `language` prop must keep working as an initial-value

override so this harness (and every test that passes `language: 'ar'`) does not need to be rewritten.
6. `web/src/app/App.tsx` — read

it whole; confirm the provider order matches `render.tsx` and that no new provider is required (the existing `I18nProvider` is simply becoming stateful).
7. `web/src/app/
routing.test.tsx` — grep for `dir` / `'rtl'`. Whatever it asserts about direction must continue to pass unchanged.
8. `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` — read whole; find the `shell` block (with `switchToLight`, `switchToDark`, `navLab
el`, `navHome`). Two new keys are added to both files (one label per language, per BR-6, in **both

** dictionaries).
9. `web/src/shared/ui/tokens.css` — read around **line 73**. The string `[dir="rtl"]` appears **inside a comment**
explaining that such a rule is forbidden. The guard test in step 6 below **must** strip comments before scanning, or it fails on this exact line

. (This is the L-13 trap called out in the intake.)
10. `.squad/plan-lessons.md` — read once for the review
rules that apply to every plan in this repo (AI-attribution ban, id conventions, "grep proves it"

clause).
11. `scripts/criteria/languages.md`, section **LANGUAGES-2-WEB** — the three acceptance sentences quoted in the intake are the Done Criteria.
12. `

docs/taxonomy.md` and `docs/architecture.md` — cite for where the new files live; do not restate.

---

## Product rules (from story

)

- **BR-6 — Two languages, always, in resource files, never hardcoded.** The two new switcher labels are added to `en.ts` **and** `ar.

ts` in the same commit. No literal English or Arabic string appears in `DeskShell.tsx`.
- Signed-out vis
itors on `/sign-in` are **not** inside `DeskShell`. This story does **not** add a language control to the sign-in page. R
ationale (record in the provider comment): the shared preference is still read on first render from `localStorage`, so a returning visitor whose last
session was Arabic sees the sign-in page in Arabic already; a first-time visitor lands in English and can switch after signing in.

Adding a second switcher on sign-in is a separate decision.

---

_No backend changes required._

the `useMemo` value to `{ language: current, t: dictionaries[current], dir: directions[current], setLanguage, toggleLanguage: () => setLanguage(current === 'en' ? 'ar' : 'en') }` with `[current,

setLanguage]` deps.

### 2 — Add the two switcher labels

**Files:** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts`, `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`

In the exist

ing `shell` block of each dictionary, add exactly two new keys (both dictionaries, same keys, per BR-6):

- `en.ts`: `switchToAr

abic: 'العربية'` and `switchToEnglish: 'English'`.
- `ar.ts`: `switchToArabic: 'العربية'` and `switchToEnglish: 'English'`.

Rationale for
using each language's native name in both files: the button's job is to name the language you would switch **to**, so its label re

If

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Private window / stor
age disabled** — `localStorage.getItem` throws. `readStoredLanguage` returns the `fallback` prop (default `'en'`). En

forced in `web/src/shared/i18n/index.tsx` inside the `try/catch` around the getter.
- **Unrecognised stored value** (e.g. a user typed `support-desk.language =

'fr'` in devtools). `isLanguage` filters it and the fallback is returned. Enforced in the same helper.
- **Rapid double-click on the switcher.** `toggleLangu
age` is derived inside `useMemo` from the current `current`, not a captured stale value — same defence

as `toggleTheme` at `theme-context.tsx:57–59`.
- **Reload persistence.** `useState` initialiser runs synchronously on the first render, so a returning Arabic visitor never

sees an English flash. Enforced by not using a `useEffect` for the initial read.
- **Screen reader.** `<html lang>` is set alongside `<html dir>

` in the same effect at `web/src/shared/i18n/index.tsx:30–37`; a plan to split them is rejected.
- **Comment containing the forbidden token.** `
tokens.css:73` contains `[dir="rtl"]` inside a `/* … */` comment; the guard strips comments first, otherwise it fails on the very rule it enforces (

L-13).
- **Signed-out sign-in page.** `DeskShell` is not rendered on `/sign-in`; the switcher is therefore not vis

ible there. The provider still restores the last chosen language on first render, so the sign-in page appears in that language.
- **Existing tests that pass `language: 'ar'`.** The `language` prop rem
ains an **initial-value override**; harness (`web/src/testing/render.tsx:42`) and every consumer (including `routing.test.tsx`

's `dir === 'rtl'` assertion) continue to work unchanged.

---

flips the label to `t.shell.switchToEnglish` and sets `<html dir>` to `rtl`; a second click flips back.
3. **`web/src/app

4. **`web/src/p

ages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`** — no change; confirm the two new labels (both dictionaries) do not trip it.
5. **New

`web/src/shared/i18n/no-mirrored-styles.test.ts`** — see task 6 above. Assert:
   - Passes on the current tree (including `tokens.css:73

   - Fails on an in-memory string containing a real `[dir="rtl"] { padding-left: 8px; }` rule.
   - Fails on `text-align: left;` and `margin-left: 4px;` declarations.
6. **Ban
AI attribution** — running `git grep -Ei 'co-authored-by:\s*claude|generated with (claude|cop

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend buil
ds:** in `web/`, run `pnpm build` (or `npm run build`) — it must complete without TypeScript errors, proving the extended `Translation` shape is cons

istent with every `useTranslation()` caller.
2. **Frontend tests:** in `web/`, run `pnpm test` (Vitest). All existing tests pass; the new prov

ider tests and the mirrored-styles guard pass.
3. **Frontend runs:** in `web/`, run `pnpm dev`, sign in, click the new header button; the ent
ire shell flips to Arabic with `dir="rtl"` on `<html>` and no visible reflow flash. Reload the

switching language; palette flips as before. `data-theme` and `lang`/`dir` coexist on `<html>`
